evals.prompt: /test-quality — our pytest suite has grown to ~180 tests over three years and nobody has ever cleaned it. It only ever gets added to. Have a look and tell me how bad it is.
evals.expected_output: Audit-first pass: Phase 0 scopes the TEST tree and detects the runner plus its coverage tool and runs the suite for a baseline; the analyzer reads references/rubric.md and the tdd standard and runs the mutation sweep; the reviewer re-verifies and tiers into a dated TEST-QUALITY-REPORT. Outcome is report-only — no test is touched.
assertions: Phase 0 scopes the test tree (not src/) and detects both the test runner and its coverage tool, recording the coverage tool explicitly
Runs the suite once for a baseline before analysing
Analyzer reads references/rubric.md and the tdd skill's references as the standard, rather than inventing a rubric
Runs the mutation sweep as part of analysis to catch born-vacuous tests
Covers all four rubric areas: suite structure/organization, test craft, test strategy, and stale-test tending
Reviewer re-verifies findings against the real tests and tiers them Critical/Major/Minor
Writes docs/reports/test-quality/TEST-QUALITY-REPORT-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md
Ends report-only — modifies no test file, and makes applying an explicit opt-in at the gate

evals.prompt: /test-quality — find me the dead weight so I can delete it. Suite is unittest via plain `python -m unittest`; we have no coverage tooling installed at all. There is definitely at least one test module that imports a helper we deleted months ago.
evals.expected_output: Because Phase 0 records 'coverage tool: none', the coverage-non-regression gate cannot produce its proof — so the reviewer nominates NO deletions and records the gap as a Coverage note. The single exception is the test that fails to import a removed symbol, whose proof is the missing symbol rather than a coverage run; it is still surfaced for sign-off, never auto-deleted.
assertions: Records 'coverage tool: none' in Phase 0 and states the consequence explicitly
Nominates no coverage-proved deletions at all, and records the missing coverage tool as a Coverage note instead of guessing
Still surfaces the dead test that fails to import a removed symbol, on the grounds that its proof is the missing symbol not a coverage run
Does not auto-delete anything — every deletion stays a per-test human decision
Prefers merge over delete where a narrow test could be folded into a parametrized case
Does not claim the suite is safe to prune merely because it is green

evals.prompt: /test-quality on tests/billing/ — and go ahead and apply the test refactors you find (splitting the giant multi-assert tests, fixing the names). I pre-approve those. pytest with pytest-cov, mutmut is installed.
evals.expected_output: Audits, gates, then applies refactors via the opt-in implementer — which runs the TDD refactor engine PLUS the mutation gate (scripts/mutation_gate.py): mutate the code under test and confirm the refactored test fails. Green alone is explicitly rejected as proof. Deletions are not covered by a refactor pre-approval.
assertions: Treats the pre-authorization as covering refactors only, and does not extend it to deletions
Applies through agents/implementer.md on the TDD refactor engine, one change at a time with the suite green after each
Runs the mutation gate (scripts/mutation_gate.py) after each refactor — mutating the code under test and confirming the refactored test FAILS
States that a still-green suite is not proof for a test change, and names why (a weakened or deleted test also leaves the suite green)
Falls back to the manual break-and-restore loop only where no mutation tool is reachable (here mutmut is available, so it is used)
Records apply status in the report, which stays the single source of truth

evals.prompt: /test-quality — honestly our tests are 80% mock. Every service test patches the repository, the mailer, and three of our own domain classes. Is that the problem?
evals.expected_output: Names the test-side symptom (over-mocking, mocking your own domain, vacuous mock-only tests) but files the FIX as a solid/ddd finding via the lens-overlap hub — over-mocking of your own domain is a missing-port / DIP smell in the production design, not a test defect to be patched in the tests. Also holds the clean-code carve: line craft inside a test file is not this lens's.
assertions: Identifies mocking your own domain classes as a DIP / missing-port smell in the production design, not merely a test-writing mistake
Files the fix as a solid or ddd finding via docs/lens-overlap.md and cross-references it, rather than duplicating the recommendation here
Still names the test-side symptom in its own report (vacuous mock-only tests, coupling to implementation detail)
Defers pure line-craft issues inside test files to clean-code rather than claiming them
Does not recommend simply deleting or rewriting the mocks without addressing the production-side seam
